{"id": 195, "title": "legalbench-rule-application pack — Client letter: Meridian Grain Cooperative evidentiary scenarios for trial preparation", "doc_type": "client_letter", "related_shape": "legalbench-rule-application", "body": "MERIDIAN GRAIN COOPERATIVE
Office of the General Counsel — Dorrance, Kansas

To our trial team at Whitlock & Deene LLP:

As we prepare for trial in the north silo fire case (Meridian Grain Cooperative v. Aldermoor Fan & Blower Co.), please screen the following three evidentiary items. For each, we state exactly what the item is and the precise purpose

args.rationale: Applying the firm's hearsay memo (FRE 801) to SCENARIO B of the Meridian Grain Cooperative client letter. Scenario B involves foreman Della Kite's out-of-court remark — "the north silo fan has been shorting for weeks" — made at the February vendor meeting to Aldermoor's regional operations manager, Petra Vosniak. The memo's test requires BOTH elements: (a) an out-of-court statement AND (b) the proponent offering it to prove the truth of the matter asserted. Here, the client letter expressly states the sole purpose is "to show the effect on the listener: that having heard the warning, Ms. Vosniak was on notice and had a duty to inspect." The client explicitly states they do not care whether the remark was accurate and are NOT offering it to prove the fan was shorting. Under Section 3(a) of the memo, an out-of-court statement offered for "effect on the listener" (to show the hearer was on notice) is a listed non-hearsay purpose. Section 4 instructs that the client's stated purpose is controlling — we must not invent an alternative purpose. Because the stated purpose is notice/effect on listener rather than truth of the matter asserted, the hearsay test is NOT satisfied. The item is not hearsay, and the determination is rejected (i.e., not admitted as hearsay for screening purposes).
